pages.description: Personal biography, background, and contact information for Kazuha Mo.

content.name: Kazuha Mo
bio: I enjoy technology, the web, and building practical things people actually use. I like exploring how simple ideas become useful tools, clean interfaces, and small projects that make everyday tasks easier.

This site is my personal space on the web — where I share a bit about myself, experiment with ideas, and collect the projects I care about. I prefer work that feels straightforward, thoughtful, and quietly useful.

Outside of classes, I'm drawn to personal projects, online services, and creating spaces that feel organized and meaningful. Over time, this site will continue to grow into a home for my tools, experiments, and things I want to keep building.

pages.title: ICS 46 Notes
pages.description: ICS 46 is UCI's data structures course, focused on implementing classic data structures in C++ and analyzing their running time and memory use.

notes.label: Lecture 0

title.zh-CN: 课程介绍、单元测试与模板

notes.summary: What ICS 46 is about, C++ unit testing with Google Test, why templates exist, function templates and compile-time instantiation, .hpp/.tpp layout, implicit type constraints, and class templates (the Box example).

notes.label: Lecture 1
notes.summary: Random number generation in C++, references, raw pointers, and an introduction to smart pointers and ownership.

notes.label: Lecture 2

title.zh-CN: 智能指针、多维数组与经验分析

notes.summary: Finishing smart-pointer ownership, 1D array review, multidimensional arrays, why we analyze algorithms, empirical timing of running time, and mathematical cost models.

notes.label: Lecture 3
notes.summary: Counting operations in 2-Sum, Big-O / Big-Ω / Big-Θ, common orders of growth, space complexity, and building an ArrayList (dynamic array) with resizing and amortized analysis.

notes.label: Lecture 4
notes.summary: Singly linked list API, implementation and analysis, doubly linked lists, ArrayList vs. linked lists, and the Stack ADT.

notes.label: Lecture 5

title.zh-CN: 队列、双端队列与栈的应用

notes.summary: Stacks on linked lists, the Queue ADT and its implementations, expression evaluation with stacks, and queue applications.

notes.label: Lecture 6
notes.summary: ADTs vs. data structures, setting up recurrences, the recursion-tree method, and the Master Theorem.

notes.label: Lecture 7
notes.summary: Circular array queues and deques, sorting basics (cost model, memory, stability), selection sort vs. insertion sort.

notes.label: Lecture 8
notes.summary: Merging sorted halves, top-down merge sort and its N log N analysis, stability and improvements, plus quick sort's background (continued in Lecture 9).

notes.label: Lecture 9
notes.summary: Quick sort: Hoare/Sedgewick 2-pointer partitioning, full traces, worst/best/average analysis, stability and in-place properties, comparison of all sorts so far, and pivot/cutoff improvements.

pages.title: CS 121 Notes
pages.description: CS 121 / IN4MATX 141 is UCI's information retrieval course: how search engines collect, process, index, and rank web documents.

notes.label: Week 1

title.en-US: Course Intro, IR and the Web, Architecture
title.zh-CN: 课程介绍、信息检索与网络、搜索引擎架构

notes.summary: How the course works, what information retrieval is, types of search engines, databases vs. search engines, relevance and retrieval models, classic vs. web IR, and search engine architecture.

notes.label: Week 2

title.en-US: The Web Corpus, SEO, Web Crawling
title.zh-CN: 网络语料、搜索引擎优化与网络爬虫

notes.summary: Corpus and tokenization, the web graph, web users and queries, the ad business model, SEO and spam, URLs, and the first steps toward a crawler.

notes.label: Week 3
notes.summary: The basic crawl loop, robots.txt and sitemaps, politeness, crawler traps, duplicates, freshness, distributed and focused crawling, and ethics, privacy and copyright.

notes.label: Week 4

title.en-US: Encodings, Storing Documents, Duplicates, Zipf's Law
title.zh-CN: 字符编码、文档存储、重复检测与 Zipf 定律

notes.summary: Document conversion and character encodings (Unicode, UTF-8), storing documents (TREC Web, compression, BigTable), exact and near-duplicate detection (checksums, n-gram fingerprints, Simhash), removing page noise, and text statistics with Zipf's law.

notes.label: Week 5

title.zh-CN: 文本处理、词项-文档矩阵

notes.summary: Tokenizing problems, stopping, stemming (suffix-s, Porter, Krovetz), phrases with POS tagging and n-grams, document structure and anchor text, and the term-document incidence matrix.

pages.title: IN4MATX 133 Notes
pages.description: IN4MATX 133 is UCI's User Interface Software course, focused on building interfaces with web technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, and modern UI frameworks.

notes.label: Lecture 1
notes.summary: Why UI implementation matters, Weiser's three waves of computing (mainframe, personal, ubiquitous), why web tools became the standard, and course goals, assignments, and policies.

notes.label: Lecture 2
notes.summary: How the web works, HTML tags, nesting, attributes, document structure and validation, screen readers and semantic elements, alt text and aria-label, and inclusive design.

notes.label: Lecture 3
notes.summary: CSS syntax and linking, element/class/ID selectors, the cascade and specificity, block vs. inline and the box model, positioning, units, pseudo-classes, fonts, and debugging tools.

notes.label: Lecture 4
notes.summary: Adaptive vs. responsive design, breakpoints and media queries, fluid grids, mobile-first, the Bootstrap grid and components, then an introduction to JavaScript's role and history.

notes.label: Lecture 5
notes.summary: Variables and types, control flow and strings, arrays, objects and JSON, functions as objects, callbacks, forEach/map/filter/reduce, and scope, hoisting, let vs. var.

notes.label: Lecture 6
notes.summary: The Document Object Model, selecting and editing elements, changing the DOM tree, events and listeners, script order, client-side validation, and package managers with npm.

notes.label: Lecture 7

title.zh-CN: TypeScript 与数据可视化工具

notes.summary: TypeScript types, classes and interfaces, tsconfig and declaration files, evaluating UI tools by threshold and ceiling, declarative visualization, and building charts with Vega-Lite.

notes.label: Lecture 8
notes.summary: Web APIs, URIs and HTTP verbs, URL escaping, AJAX with XML vs. JSON, XMLHttpRequest vs. fetch(), asynchronous requests, promises with .then()/.catch(), the same-origin policy, and Promise.all.

notes.label: Lecture 9

title.zh-CN: 服务器端开发、身份验证与授权

notes.summary: Node.js and npm, reading files, Express and its generator, authentication vs. authorization, OAuth 2.0 and its four steps, the same-origin policy, and OpenID Connect.

notes.label: Lecture 10
notes.summary: Frameworks for large clients, installing Angular, Model-View-Controller and how Angular implements it, components and the root component, interpolation/property/event/two-way binding, @if and @for, and nesting components with inputs and outputs.

pages.title: ICS 45C Notes
pages.description: ICS 45C is UCI's C++ programming course, focused on how programs are designed, built, debugged, and reasoned about in a lower-level language.

notes.label: Week 1
notes.summary: Runestone + LearnCpp + GoogleTest primer notes, organized into one structured reading guide.

notes.label: Week 2
notes.summary: References, OOP fundamentals, classes, constructors, C arrays, and more — integrated reading notes for Week 2.

notes.label: Week 3
notes.summary: std::string, return by reference, C-style arrays and pointer arithmetic, operator overloading, file I/O, and error handling.

notes.label: Week 4
notes.summary: Literals, constexpr, dynamic memory (new/delete), copy/move constructors, Rule of Three/Five, and the IntList example.

notes.label: Week 5
notes.summary: Linked lists (Node, UnorderedList, CharList), namespace list helpers, RAII for linked structures, and the Three Laws of Recursion (Tower of Hanoi, maze, Sierpinski).

notes.label: Week 6
notes.summary: Inheritance and polymorphism: is-a, derived constructors, public/protected/private inheritance, virtual functions, pure virtual & abstract classes, dynamic_cast, and printing inherited classes via operator<<.

notes.label: Week 7
notes.summary: Templates (function & class), non-type template parameters, lambdas and captures, exceptions (throw/try/catch, stack unwinding, exception classes, noexcept), friend non-member functions, stringstreams, and multiple inheritance with virtual base classes.

notes.label: Week 8
notes.summary: The C++ Standard Library and STL — containers (sequence, associative, adapter), iterators and iterator categories, algorithms (sort/find/transform/accumulate…), iterator adapters (back_inserter, stream iterators, reverse iterators), function objects, C++20 ranges, and the iostream library (istream/ostream, manipulators, formatting flags).

notes.label: Week 9
notes.summary: Designing container classes (IntArray full build-up), std::initializer_list and brace-vs-paren initialization, assert / static_assert / NDEBUG, iterators in depth (begin/end, invalidation, the erase idiom), std::iterator_traits and iterator category tags, smart pointers and move semantics (unique_ptr, shared_ptr, make_unique/make_shared), C++20 ranges and views, and HW9 SetList + MapArray with their forward / random-access iterators.

notes.label: Final Review
notes.summary: Exam-ready review built from the 109-question study guide and every lecture deck — all 13 topic groups (C++ programs, variables & expressions, memory/lifetime/scope, arrays/strings/linked lists, functions & parameters, classes & objects, inheritance & polymorphism, templates, lambdas, exceptions, namespaces, I/O streams, STL containers/iterators/algorithms), plus quick comparison tables, a code-review appendix, and the 12 most important things to walk in knowing.

pages.title: IN4MATX 43 Notes
pages.description: IN4MATX 43 introduces software engineering through the people, processes, and tools behind real-world software systems.

notes.label: Week 1
notes.summary: An overview of what software engineering is, why software matters, and the core principles that shape the rest of the course.

notes.label: Week 2
notes.summary: Software failures, why requirements matter, requirements analysis and specification, the requirements document, specification methods, and Ziv's Law.

notes.label: Week 3

title.en-US: Use Cases and Software Engineering Ethics

notes.summary: Use cases, actors, basic/alternative/exception flows, use case diagrams and models, plus the ACM/IEEE Software Engineering Code of Ethics.

notes.label: Week 4
notes.summary: Why architecture matters, its elements, prescriptive vs. descriptive views, architectural erosion, and the six architectural styles.

notes.label: Week 5
notes.summary: From architecture to detailed design, the six design approaches, abstraction, UML class diagrams (associations, multiplicity, aggregation vs. composition), cohesion, coupling, and information hiding.

notes.label: Week 6

title.zh-CN: 以用户为中心的设计与可用性

notes.summary: How to make software that meets the user's needs: why usability matters, the eight user-centered design methods (interviews, personas, scenarios, storyboards, wireframes, design guidelines, heuristic evaluation, user testing), and Nielsen's ten heuristics.

notes.label: Week 7
notes.summary: How do we know the software works? Verification vs. validation, the four QA technique families, the basic testing process, IEEE testing terminology (mistake/fault/error/failure), the three levels of testing (unit/integration/system), six ways to choose test cases, test oracles, and how to know when we're done testing.

notes.label: Week 8

title.en-US: Test Case Selection — Black-Box, White-Box, and Other QA Techniques
title.zh-CN: 测试用例的选取——黑盒、白盒与其他质量保证方法

notes.summary: How do we actually choose test cases? Black-box (specification-based) testing with equivalence class partitioning and boundary value analysis, combinatorial testing, white-box (structural) testing with control-flow graphs and coverage criteria (statement / branch / condition / path), plus inspections and code reviews, formal methods, static analysis, and the Quiz 7 study guide.

notes.label: Week 9

title.en-US: Software Process and Life Cycle Models
title.zh-CN: 软件流程与生命周期模型

notes.summary: From testing to process: why software engineering needs a defined process, what a model is, and the eight life cycle models (build-and-fix, waterfall, rapid prototyping, incremental, spiral, RUP, XP, Agile/Scrum) — including the fourteen XP practices, the Agile Manifesto and its principles, Ziv's Law, a side-by-side comparison of all models, and the Quiz 9 / final exam study guide.

notes.label: Final Review
notes.summary: Cumulative, exam-ready review organized as eight "big questions" mapped to each weekly quiz: what software engineering is (No Silver Bullet, the four essential difficulties), requirements, use cases, professional ethics (ACM code), software architecture and the six architectural styles, detailed design with UML class diagrams, user-centered design and Nielsen's ten heuristics, and software testing (black-box/white-box, coverage criteria) — plus the eight process models, a one-page cheat sheet, the top-ten exam traps, and a knowledge tree.
